title: Sculpture & Antiquity
description: Marble, bronze, and stone — the enduring forms of the ancient and classical world.
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Sabine Houdon (1787–1836)
items.medium: White marble on gray marble socle
items.description_narrative: This white marble portrait captures Sabine Houdon, daughter of the acclaimed sculptor Jean Antoine Houdon. Created in 1788, it reflects the artist's masterful ability to render lifelike forms in stone.
items.tags: sculpture, portrait, marble, neoclassical, child, french art, 18th century
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Standing Figure with Jeweled Headdress
items.medium: Gypsum plaster; modeled, carved, polychrome-painted, gilded
items.description_narrative: This gypsum plaster sculpture depicts a standing figure adorned with a jeweled headdress, showcasing intricate modeling, carving, polychrome-painting, and gilding. Created between the 12th and early 13th centuries, this work is a testament to the artistry of its unknown maker.
items.tags: figure, sculpture, medieval, gypsum, jeweled, headdress, polychrome, gilded
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Bronze figure of a boy in Eastern dress
items.description_narrative: This bronze figure depicts a young boy adorned in Eastern dress, showcasing the intricate details of his attire. It is a remarkable example of ancient metalwork from the Hellenistic or early Roman period.
items.tags: bronze, figure, boy, eastern dress, ancient, greek, roman, sculpture
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Bronze statuette of a philosopher on a lamp stand
items.description_narrative: This bronze statuette depicts a philosopher, designed to adorn a lamp stand. Dating from the late 1st century BCE, it exemplifies Roman decorative arts.
items.tags: bronze, statuette, philosopher, lamp stand, roman, ancient, sculpture, decorative art
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Marble torso of a boy
items.description_narrative: This marble torso depicts a young boy, possibly a deity or athlete, rendered with the refined skill characteristic of its era. Though the artist remains unknown, the work stands as a testament to the classical sculptural traditions of the Roman world.
items.tags: roman, sculpture, marble, torso, boy, ancient, classical
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Limestone statue of Aphrodite holding winged Eros
items.description_narrative: This Cypriot limestone statue depicts the goddess Aphrodite cradling the winged figure of Eros. Dating to the late 4th century BCE, it reflects a common Hellenistic artistic theme.
items.tags: goddess, sculpture, ancient, cypriot, mythological, eros, aphrodite, classical
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Marble portrait of the co-emperor Lucius Verus
items.description_narrative: This marble portrait depicts Lucius Verus, co-emperor of Rome from 161 to 169 CE. It exemplifies the sculptural artistry and imperial representation characteristic of the Roman period.
items.tags: roman, portrait, sculpture, marble, emperor, imperial
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Marble portrait bust of a woman
items.description_narrative: This marble portrait bust captures the likeness of a Roman woman from the turn of the 3rd century CE. Expertly carved from marble, it exemplifies the detailed sculptural tradition of the Roman Empire.
items.tags: portrait, woman, marble, bust, roman, ancient, sculpture
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Venus de Milo
items.description_narrative: The Venus de Milo is an iconic ancient Greek marble statue, renowned for its depiction of the goddess Aphrodite. Discovered on the island of Milos, its missing arms contribute to its enduring mystery and beauty.
items.tags: greek, hellenistic, sculpture, marble, goddess, aphrodite, classical, nude, antiquity
items.credit_line: Ancient Greek Marble Aphrodite of Milos (Venus de Milo), 130-100 BC

items.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace
items.description_narrative: This monumental marble sculpture depicts Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, poised dramatically as if descending from the sky. Discovered in the Sanctuary of the Great Gods on Samothrace, it celebrates a naval triumph and is renowned for its dynamic composition and masterful drapery.
items.tags: ancient greek, hellenistic, sculpture, nike, victory, marble, dramatic, movement

items.title: Laocoön and His Sons
items.description_narrative: This monumental marble sculpture captures the dramatic struggle of the Trojan priest Laocoön and his two sons as they are attacked by sea serpents, a scene from the Trojan War myth. Its intricate composition and intense depiction of suffering exemplify Hellenistic art's mastery of human anatomy and emotion.
items.tags: hellenistic, classical, mythology, sculpture, struggle, suffering, ancient greek, dramatic

items.title: Pietà
items.description_narrative: This monumental marble sculpture depicts the Virgin Mary cradling the body of Jesus after his crucifixion, a poignant representation of sorrow and maternal love. Carved by Michelangelo, it is renowned for its harmonious composition and idealized forms, conveying profound emotion through a highly polished finish.
items.tags: sculpture, renaissance, christian art, religious, marble, virgin mary, jesus, lamentation, italian

items.title: Moses
items.description_narrative: Michelangelo's monumental marble sculpture captures Moses in a moment of intense emotion, holding the Tablets of the Law. This powerful work was intended as a central figure for the tomb of Pope Julius II.
items.tags: biblical, high renaissance, sculpture, marble, monumental, old testament, italian

items.title: Discobolus
items.description_narrative: Myron's iconic Discobolus captures an athlete in the moment before releasing a discus, showcasing the ideal of physical prowess and dynamic tension. Though the original bronze is lost, its form is preserved through numerous Roman marble copies, illustrating the artistic and athletic ideals of classical Greece.
items.tags: ancient greek, sculpture, athlete, classical art, idealized form, movement, human form, roman copy

items.title: The Thinker
items.description_narrative: Auguste Rodin's iconic sculpture, "The Thinker," depicts a monumental nude male figure seated in deep contemplation. Originally conceived to crown his ambitious "Gates of Hell," this powerful work has become a universal symbol of intellectual ponderance and human struggle.
items.tags: contemplation, sculpture, male nude, symbolism, monumental, pensive, realism

items.title: The Kiss
items.description_narrative: Auguste Rodin's iconic sculpture, "The Kiss," captures a passionate embrace between two figures. The work is celebrated for its sensual depiction of human emotion and physical connection.
items.tags: sculpture, marble, love, passion, embrace, sensuality, Symbolism, French art
